name: Hydrogen
description: The lightest element, it makes up about three quarters of the ordinary matter in the universe.

name: Helium
description: Found in the Sun's spectrum before it was found on Earth, it stays liquid down to absolute zero at normal pressure.

name: Lithium
description: The lightest metal, it floats on water and powers most rechargeable batteries.

name: Beryllium
description: Light and stiff, it lets X-rays through and was used for the mirrors of the James Webb Space Telescope.

name: Boron
description: Added to glass, it makes the heat-resistant borosilicate kind used in laboratories and kitchens.

name: Carbon
description: The basis of all known life, it forms soft graphite and hard diamond alike.

name: Nitrogen
description: It makes up about 78 percent of the air we breathe.

name: Oxygen
description: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust, it fills the air thanks to billions of years of photosynthesis.

name: Fluorine
description: The most reactive of all elements, it protects teeth as fluoride in toothpaste.

name: Neon
description: It glows reddish orange in an electric discharge, the light of the first neon signs.

name: Sodium
description: A soft metal that reacts violently with water, it is half of table salt.

name: Magnesium
description: It burns with a brilliant white light and sits at the heart of every chlorophyll molecule.

name: Aluminium
description: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust, it was so hard to extract that it was once prized like gold.

name: Silicon
description: The second most abundant element in the Earth's crust, it is the material of computer chips.

name: Phosphorus
description: First isolated from urine in 1669, its white form glows faintly in the dark.

name: Sulfur
description: Known since ancient times as brimstone, it burns with a blue flame.

name: Chlorine
description: A yellow-green gas, it keeps drinking water and swimming pools free of germs.

name: Argon
description: The third most abundant gas in the air, it fills light bulbs to protect their filaments.

name: Potassium
description: Essential to every nerve signal, it gives bananas their reputation.

name: Calcium
description: The most abundant metal in the human body, it builds bones and teeth.

name: Scandium
description: Predicted by Mendeleev before its discovery, it strengthens the aluminium of bicycle frames.

name: Titanium
description: As strong as steel at nearly half the weight, it is used in aircraft and medical implants.

name: Vanadium
description: Named after a Norse goddess of beauty, it makes steel tools tougher.

name: Chromium
description: It gives rubies their red and stainless steel its resistance to rust.

name: Manganese
description: Essential to making steel, it also helps plants split water during photosynthesis.

name: Iron
description: The most common element on Earth by mass, most of it lies in the planet's core.

name: Cobalt
description: It has coloured glass and ceramics deep blue for thousands of years.

name: Nickel
description: One of the few elements that are magnetic at room temperature, it makes up part of the Earth's core.

name: Copper
description: One of the first metals people worked, it still carries most of the world's electricity.

name: Zinc
description: A coat of it keeps steel from rusting, a process called galvanizing.

name: Gallium
description: It melts at about 30 °C, so it turns liquid in the palm of a hand.

name: Germanium
description: Predicted by Mendeleev, it was the material of the first transistor.

name: Arsenic
description: Long known as a poison, it is now used in fast semiconductors such as gallium arsenide.

name: Selenium
description: Named after the Moon, it conducts electricity better in light than in darkness.

name: Bromine
description: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature, it smells strongly.

name: Krypton
description: A rare gas of the air, it defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983.

name: Rubidium
description: Named after the red lines of its spectrum, it keeps time in atomic clocks.

name: Strontium
description: It gives fireworks and flares their bright red.

name: Yttrium
description: One of four elements named after the Swedish village of Ytterby, it makes the red in old colour televisions.

name: Zirconium
description: It barely absorbs neutrons, so it clads the fuel rods of nuclear reactors.

name: Niobium
description: Named after Niobe, daughter of Tantalus, it makes the superconducting magnets of MRI scanners.

name: Molybdenum
description: It melts at over 2600 °C and strengthens steel at high temperatures.

name: Technetium
description: The first element made artificially, it is used in millions of medical scans each year.

name: Ruthenium
description: Named after Russia, it hardens platinum and palladium.

name: Rhodium
description: One of the rarest and costliest metals, it cleans car exhaust in catalytic converters.

name: Palladium
description: It can soak up hundreds of times its own volume of hydrogen.

name: Silver
description: It conducts electricity and heat better than any other element.

name: Cadmium
description: It gives artists' paints their bright yellows and reds.

name: Indium
description: Soft enough to cut with a knife, it makes the transparent electrodes of touch screens.

name: Tin
description: Mixed with copper, it made the bronze that named an age.

name: Antimony
description: Ancient Egyptians used its sulfide as the black eye cosmetic kohl.

name: Tellurium
description: Named after the Earth, it is used in rewritable discs and solar panels.

name: Iodine
description: Its crystals turn straight into a violet vapour, and the thyroid gland needs it.

name: Xenon
description: Named from the Greek for stranger, it lights car headlamps and drives ion engines in space.

name: Caesium
description: Its atoms define the second, the base of all atomic clocks.

name: Barium
description: Swallowed as a sulfate, it makes the gut visible on X-rays.

name: Lanthanum
description: The first of the lanthanides, it makes camera lenses sharper.

name: Cerium
description: The most abundant rare earth, it makes the sparks of lighter flints.

name: Praseodymium
description: It colours glass a yellow-green and goes into welders' goggles.

name: Neodymium
description: It makes the strongest permanent magnets, found in headphones and electric motors.

name: Promethium
description: Named after Prometheus, it is the only lanthanide with no stable form.

name: Samarium
description: The first element named after a person, it makes magnets that work at high temperatures.

name: Europium
description: Named after Europe, it glows red under ultraviolet light and guards euro banknotes against forgery.

name: Gadolinium
description: It brightens tissues in MRI scans and is magnetic below about 20 °C.

name: Terbium
description: Another element named after Ytterby, it gives screens and lamps their green.

name: Dysprosium
description: Named from the Greek for hard to get, it keeps magnets strong in electric car motors.

name: Holmium
description: Named after Stockholm, it has the highest magnetic strength of any element.

name: Erbium
description: It amplifies the light that carries data through optical fibres.

name: Thulium
description: Named after Thule, a mythical far north, it is among the rarest lanthanides.

name: Ytterbium
description: The fourth element named after Ytterby, it keeps time in some of the most precise atomic clocks.

name: Lutetium
description: Named after Lutetia, the Roman name of Paris, it is the last and densest lanthanide.

name: Hafnium
description: Named after Copenhagen, it absorbs neutrons in the control rods of reactors.

name: Tantalum
description: Named after Tantalus of Greek myth, it makes the small capacitors in phones.

name: Tungsten
description: It has the highest melting point of any metal and lit the filaments of light bulbs.

name: Rhenium
description: The last stable element to be discovered, in 1925, it goes into jet engine blades.

name: Osmium
description: The densest natural element, it was once used for fountain pen tips.

name: Iridium
description: A layer of it in rocks 66 million years old marks the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.

name: Platinum
description: It barely corrodes, and it speeds up reactions in car exhaust and fuel cells.

name: Gold
description: It never tarnishes, and all the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about 22 metres wide.

name: Mercury
description: The only metal that is liquid at room temperature, it once filled thermometers.

name: Thallium
description: Named after the green line of its spectrum, it is highly toxic.

name: Lead
description: Dense and soft, it shields X-ray rooms, and the Romans made water pipes of it.

name: Bismuth
description: It forms iridescent stepped crystals and soothes upset stomachs.

name: Polonium
description: Discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie, it was named after Poland.

name: Astatine
description: The rarest element that occurs in nature, only a few grams of it exist in the Earth's crust at any time.

name: Radon
description: A radioactive gas that seeps from the ground, it can gather in cellars.

name: Francium
description: Discovered in 1939 by Marguerite Perey, it was the last element found in nature.

name: Radium
description: Discovered by the Curies, it once made watch dials glow in the dark.

name: Actinium
description: Named from the Greek for ray, it gives the actinides their name and glows blue in the dark.

name: Thorium
description: Named after Thor, it is about three times as abundant as uranium.

name: Protactinium
description: One of the rarest natural elements, it decays into actinium.

name: Uranium
description: The heaviest element found in nature in quantity, it fuels nuclear power stations.

name: Neptunium
description: The first element beyond uranium, made in 1940, it was named after the planet Neptune.

name: Plutonium
description: Named after Pluto, it powers space probes such as Voyager and New Horizons.

name: Americium
description: Named after the Americas, a tiny amount of it sits in most smoke detectors.

name: Curium
description: Named after Marie and Pierre Curie, it was the radiation source of instruments on Mars rovers.

name: Berkelium
description: Named after Berkeley, California, where it was first made in 1949.

name: Californium
description: A strong source of neutrons, it helps start nuclear reactors and find gold and oil.

name: Einsteinium
description: Named after Albert Einstein, it was first found in the debris of a hydrogen bomb test.

name: Fermium
description: Named after Enrico Fermi, it is the heaviest element that can be made by bombarding lighter ones with neutrons.

name: Mendelevium
description: Named after Dmitri Mendeleev, the father of the periodic table.

name: Nobelium
description: Named after Alfred Nobel, its discovery was disputed for decades.

name: Lawrencium
description: Named after Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron, it closes the actinide row.

name: Rutherfordium
description: Named after Ernest Rutherford, it is the first of the superheavy elements.

name: Dubnium
description: Named after Dubna, the Russian town where it was made.

name: Seaborgium
description: Named after Glenn Seaborg, who was still alive when it got his name.

name: Bohrium
description: Named after Niels Bohr, only a few atoms of it have ever been made.

name: Hassium
description: Named after the German state of Hesse, it is thought to be denser than osmium.

name: Meitnerium
description: Named after Lise Meitner, who helped explain nuclear fission.

name: Darmstadtium
description: Named after the German city of Darmstadt, its atoms last only seconds.

name: Roentgenium
description: Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, the discoverer of X-rays.

name: Copernicium
description: Named after Nicolaus Copernicus, it may be a liquid or a gas at room temperature.

name: Nihonium
description: Named after Japan, it was the first element discovered in Asia.

name: Flerovium
description: Named after the Flerov Laboratory in Dubna, it may behave almost like a noble gas.

name: Moscovium
description: Named after the Moscow region, its atoms last a fraction of a second.

name: Livermorium
description: Named after Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California.

name: Tennessine
description: Named after Tennessee, it was among the last four elements to be named, in 2016.

name: Oganesson
description: The heaviest element known, it is named after the physicist Yuri Oganessian.
